item.text: I’ll inspect the repository guidance and the current tracing/server code, then write the required checkpoint before editing. I’ll keep the change focused on extracting tracing setup and wiring its lifecycle into gRPC startup.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "mkdir -p .codex-role-output && cat > .codex-role-output/checkpoint.md <<'EOF'
# Checkpoint

Task: Extract tracing resource, provider, and exporter construction from gRPC startup into "'`internal/tracing`, then wire provider/exporter shutdown into the gRPC server lifecycle.

Requirements being tracked:
- Build an environment-aware OpenTelemetry resource with Flipt service name/version.
- Provide an always-on tracer provider constructor.
- Support Jaeger, Zipkin, and OTLP exporters, including accepted OTLP endpoint schemes and configured headers; return exporter shutdown.
- Make exporter construction safe across repeated invocations and report unsupported exporters/endpoints clearly.
- Use the tracing package from gRPC startup and register shutdowns in the existing lifecycle sequence.

Initial status: repository inspection pending.
EOF
find .. -name AGENTS.md -print; find internal -maxdepth 4 -type f '"\\( -name 'grpc.go' -o -path '*/tracing/*' \\) -print; git status --short"

Implemented the tracing extraction in [tracing.go](/app/internal/tracing/tracing.go). It builds an environment-aware resource and always-sampling provider, and creates independent Jaeger, Zipkin, or OTLP exporters with shutdown functions. OTLP accepts the requested endpoint formats, applies configured headers, and reports invalid endpoints clearly.

[gRPC startup](/app/internal/cmd/grpc.go:154) now uses the tracing package and registers provider and exporter shutdowns in the server lifecycle. The existing exporter test now calls the extracted API.
